_about: Bug fixes since the baseline commit and the regression tests that exercise each, checked by
A regression test is a test added or changed in the fix commit, or named in its message.
untested_parts names a part of a fix that no test exercises.

rule.selects: every commit since the baseline whose subject or body (trailers removed) matches message_pattern, case-insensitive, and every commit that adds an entry under a '### Fixed' heading of CHANGELOG.md
rule.definition: A bug fix corrects behaviour of shipped code, scripts, tests or CI that was wrong before the commit, including messages the code prints. Documentation-only corrections, new features, evidence re-freezes and new tests of behaviour that was already right are not bug fixes.
rule.review: Every selected commit is either a fix mapped to regression tests (test node ids that must exist) or an exclusion with a reason. A fix the rule misses is added by hand with selected_by: manual. A fix with no test stays listed, with no_test_reason, and is reported as open.

fixes.bug: The wheel-content test skipped when the wheel failed to build, so a broken build passed as a skip.

The Constitutive Jacobian screen's preview said '(none found)' for a routine that assigns DDSDDE once before the stress update reads it (the FCC crystal routine); it now says which block is replaced, which assignment is kept and where the extraction goes.

A labelled IF on a promoted variable lost its statement label (the GOTO target vanished and the file did not compile in Abaqus), and the inputs of DDSDDE writes that feed the predictor stress were dropped, so the transformed stress differed from the original's by a hydrostatic offset.

A DATA-initialised, never-assigned name that the contract listed under promote stayed promoted and the DATA blocker then refused the file, so UMAT_HIN could not be transformed from its own benchmark contract.
UMAT_PCO's committed benchmark contract failed the transform because its helper routines live in sibling files the contract could not name; a compact contract may now declare dependency_roots.

The provider verifier drove every model along the fixed J2 check path (the ten-parameter FCC provider went non-finite there), and the provider objects and Mapping.json carried the developer's build directory. The code and tests are in the preceding work-in-progress commits 55a870e, 421173d and 98a2f28, which this commit validates.

Run from an installed package, the developer screens' default workspace resolved inside the Python environment's lib directory (four levels above the module), and the uniaxial check path failed on a missing parameter_sensitivity/loading_paths.json instead of saying the file is not installed.
An assignment to a kept-real variable whose right-hand side reads a promoted value was rewritten from its first physical line only ('EMOD = REAL(A + B *)'), leaving the continuation line dangling.
The parameter-sensitivity sweep ran plain 'make'; GNU make predefines FC=f77, so the generated Makefile's 'FC ?= gfortran' never applied and the OTI driver build failed wherever f77 is absent.

The transformed UMAT_HIN passed hypercomplex values where its lifted helpers expect integers and reals where they expect hypercomplex values (INTEGER variables were promoted and the lifted bodies' IMPLICIT types were not read); gfortran 10 refused it and the stress was 63 % off the original's. Its generated Makefiles kept GNU make's built-in FC=f77, because 'FC ?= gfortran' never applies; they now replace that default and keep a caller's FC.

The contract packaging tests imported tomllib, which Python 3.10 lacks, and the wheel test skipped on every 3.12 run because setuptools was not declared; a docstring quoting a Windows path raised an invalid-escape SyntaxWarning; and the clean-clone acceptance run piped pytest through tail, so a failure printed the end of one assertion message without naming the failing test.
codemeta.json claimed Linux, Windows and macOS and pyproject.toml 'OS Independent', while only Linux is tested.

An Abaqus job whose compile line could not find ifort was classified as 'the console kept no compiler diagnostic', which blames the UMAT; and streamlit run src/umat_oti/app/unified_app.py opened an empty page because the module never called main().

A local-Jacobian request did not promote the variable it replaces: with DF=ONE the extraction went to an undeclared DF_OTI, the Newton update divided by an unassigned DF, and the transform reported success with stresses 4.6 % off.
The legacy validation runner recognised only bash's 'ifort: command not found' (dash prints 'ifort: not found'), and reproduce.py reported '(clean)' when git could not read the tree at all.

Lifting and derivative defects of a gradient-driven transform silently gave wrong numbers or a file that would not build: a COMMON member retyped in a lifted helper, a repeated INCLUDE constant, a continued CALL left pointing at the untransformed routine, an integer array constructor handed to MATMUL, infinite partials turning into NaN, and a repeated eigenvalue cluster refused instead of averaged.

The only provider entry point set DFGRD0 = DFGRD1 = I, so a UMAT that reads its kinematics from the deformation gradient returned zero stress for every increment without any failure; DSPEVD also returned NaN with INFO = 0 for a tiny off-diagonal (OFFVAL*OFFVAL underflow) and for a diagonal matrix lost its eigenvector derivatives.

The family denominators published since pass14 came from the keyword classification nobody had reviewed while the report named only the file, so an unreviewed denominator could be quoted as a reviewed one; the report now digests the file and prints the reviewed coverage beside each count.

A state shadow that was declared, zeroed, read and written but never copied in nor out compiled and returned a stress computed from an all-zero state (140 of 140 increments of one corpus source); and every integer exponent of a promoted expression was emitted as a real power (Y_OTI**2 became Y_OTI**2.0D0), which Fortran defines only for a non-negative base.

The dependency bundler copied a stub ABA_PARAM.INC into dependencies/ and pointed the include there, a path an Abaqus job directory does not have (140 of 234 pass17 rows stopped at the compile); implicitly typed PROPS copies lost their derivative, binary32 variables were rounded or widened, STRESS/DDSDDE extraction was skipped on branch paths, a zero-base power lost its zero primal, and a build that stopped working was not said.
The NTENS rule treated a DO loop bounded at 3 as plane stress without a shear at index 3, so the Lemaitre UMAT had been verified on a layout that put a shear in the sigma_33 slot.

The licence classifier read the body of a licence, so every GNU text was misread (the GPL-3.0 text names Affero in section 13; GPL-2.0 and LGPL-2.1 read as LGPL-3.0), registry bytes was the decoded length instead of the file size and companion lists were truncated.

The RA /2 adapter copied RA's prose reference into the enumerated reference field and wrote a non-schema rule id, so the published manifest failed its own schema; the packaging test's wheel build also needed the network.

The routine-level harness drove every source at COORDS = 0 (position-dependent originals went non-finite and read inconclusive), aborted a whole source when the original STOPped on one path, and a relative --out made every original 'not build'.

A lifted helper read the host's PARAMETER TWO as an uninitialised local (wrong stress in UVCmultiaxial/UVCuniaxial_IS); a seed on a continued CALL line was not seen; a call omitting an OPTIONAL argument of a lifted helper compiled and read the stack.
The manifest's primal cell carried the FE-comparison ratio (informational since D-15) as max_error, e.g. 1.9e6 on a cell the primal gate verified.
The harness and campaign tests hard-coded this machine's workspace path, and the published manifest carried machine paths.
An original that STOPped under a perturbation left unwritten records that the harness indexed, aborting the whole source; unapplied isolation probes did not block derivative verdicts explicitly.

Primal cells labelled process failures and undefined-in-original outputs as 'failed' with a non-deciding ratio; D-18's run selection existed only as --merge order; _portable replaced inside longer names.

A case's reference could drop judged states or whole paths with its sha refreshed and still pass; a path missing from the reference crashed; zero_pass ignored the stored value; the tier printed 'canaries all rejected' when one was not; the licence guard trusted case.json.

Host constants were carried per statement (a shadowing local dropped them all: wrong stress), internal procedures were typed default REAL, named constants were typed by their value's form (REAL constants lost binary32, INTEGER typing made 1/THREE integer division), integer quotients were promoted, and statement functions/ENTRY produced uncompilable output reported as success.

The transform summary (and gradient-alias record and derivative manifest) named the staged bundle copy as 'source' instead of the author's file, so the regression service's rows, keyed on it, stopped matching the contracts that asked for them (since 57eaeff).

The registry builder copied the batch row's compiled flag onto refused sources (9 read transformed False, compiled True), and gave not_a_umat sources the transform's refusal text as their reason, as though the refusal decided the verdict.

The shared residual_fixture_v1 schema closed finite_history.evidence without listing primal_decided_by, which the verifier writes since 4d91f0c and the exporter carries verbatim, so every fixture frozen at the current generation was refused by its own producer's contract (contract 4.1.0 declares it).

A literal or REAL expression handed to a lifted helper's hypercomplex dummy compiled through the implicit interface and the callee read the derivative parts from beyond the temporary (czmHealing.f, UMAT_MohrCoulomb.f; a toy's DDSDDE(1,2) 312.09 against FD 312.00), and real_arguments_into_oti_helper_dummies skipped such actuals.
DDSDDE writes inside a lifted callee, which land in DDSDDE_OTI, were refused as uncovered old-tangent writes (seven corpus sources).

A shadow's extent came from the file-wide scanner row, so a UMAT array named like a helper's scalar dummy was refused for having no shape; a keyword argument name was read as a use of the caller's variable.
A FORALL that only symmetrises the old tangent, directly after the output region, was refused as an uncovered DDSDDE write.

A REAL statement reading the seed into a promoted variable could be left ahead of the seed block, losing that variable's derivative with a bitwise-correct stress (DDSDDE(1,2) 1000.0 against FD 1040.8); now refused by a semantic check.

The dependency resolver skipped fixed-form definitions written after a tab in the label field as continuation lines, so the companion search reported routines missing from the files that define them (all five OXFORD-UMAT copies); GETRANK was not known as an Abaqus runtime routine; module variables on the stress path were refused as an unreadable module.
The DATA-shadow guard read DATA statements of every routine, refusing a UMAT whose promoted local shares a name with a DATA-initialised local of another routine (damin225 FACTOR, ReachOptimum A1).

demanded() saw only literal and bare-identifier PROPS subscripts, so an index expression (UVC props((N_BASIC_PROPS - 1) + 2 * i)) left the demand exact at PROPS(1:7) and the author's 11-constant decks were rejected as another parameterisation; a literal-bounded DO loop over PROPS(I) was not counted.

When every block was rejected the reason quoted the first six rejections in scan order, so the author's own README-named block (mholla iso_Mandel: *DEPVAR 3 against STATEV(5)) could be left out of it.
The seed-read semantic check caught one hop only; a seed read reaching a shadowed name through a REAL intermediate (T = DSTRAN(2); G = PROPS(1)*(1+T)) still transformed with a wrong DDSDDE.

A tab inside the fixed-form label field but not in column 1 was read as a continuation line by the emitter and the lifter, gluing two statements together (MODIFIED_JC.f, UMAT_visco_FGJD_2026.for, wellbore.f did not compile).
A REAL initialised in its declaration was retyped to the OTI type with a REAL initializer, and a fixed-form ': :' was emitted literally; both stopped the build (UMAT_visco/viscohybrid_FGJD_2026.for).
A supplied solver utility (ROTSIG) called outside the stress interval with a shadowed argument was not lifted, and the source was refused by the leak check (UMATPlasticity.f).
A REAL argument of a mixed MIN/MAX was given the OTI type as (arg) + 0.0D0*(anchor), which turned -0.0 into +0.0 when the anchor's real part was positive (primal differs from the original).
The PARAMETER promotion of a declaration-initialised REAL missed a write through a function reference (X = BUMP(TEN)); the lifted helper then wrote a PARAMETER (SIGSEGV under gfortran).

Two tests passed regardless of the behaviour they claimed to check: the ROTSIG test read STATEV out of bounds with a zero DROT, and the signed-zero test compiled a hard-coded wrap instead of the emitted one.

The Abaqus tangent gate verified on best-relative-per-entry against a 1e-6 tolerance with 2-step plateaus, chose states from the transformed history and on the flattened point list, took the author's tangent and a one-sided branch difference as verdicts, and used the increment as the step scale (Curie B7 tangent_not_verified diagnosis, Vera A1-A8).
cells.fold merged the cells of different D-21 parameter sets of one source, and resolve_entry resolved a bare key of a multi-set plan to its first set and resolved refused plans (Vera's G review C6).

A council row's kinematics and ceiling were recorded as author_published, identical parameter sets were accepted as independent, and a documented domain stated in words was dropped without a mark (Vera's G review C2, C4, C5).
corpus_cases freeze wrapper rejected new FeatureTally.add keywords (kinematic_input, block_derivative, double_zero) added by G4/G10, so freezing any case raised TypeError.

The Abaqus gate paired records across steps (increment restarts each step), fd.judge_column's value-under-test round-off divided |F|-sized terms by the increment so a 1e-4 defect passed under quad, and the A6 shrink rule could clear a kink (Vera G10 review B1, B2, A6).

The gate re-selected states on every run instead of using a row's frozen states, did not prefer an activating integration point, and failed a row whose seed map could not be read (Vera G10 review A5, A8).

The lifter stitched fixed-form continuations with a blank, splitting a name broken across lines (G3 / 1 read as G3 1) and the Jeff97 Petal and SeaShell provider builds failed; character literals across a break lost the compilers' column layout.

ddsdde_legacy_gate labelled every non-verified Abaqus tangent 'failed' (an unresolved row such as 26606e08 read as a measured disagreement), the registry did not read the D-4 gate's tangent.failed, the corpus page and plain language said 'could not pin the tangent down' / 'did not settle' over rows whose gate measured a disagreement, and a council row with no council_sets could count (Vera's final review before pass21).

The D-4 zero rule failed an exact zero in both precisions against a 1e-27 OTI residue (pass21 A3 false FAIL); Vera's floor NOISE_FACTOR*eps*max(S,|block derivative|), times the increment count for total derivatives and capped at RESOLUTION*S, now bounds the zero branch, while 1e-6*S still fails.

A quad replay staged the author's double-precision INCLUDE files as links, so its reference was mixed-precision (davidmorin UMAT_MODEL.f, jpsferreira PARAM_UMAT.INC; Vera B10 condition A); an absolute or .. INCLUDE was staged from outside the source tree (condition B).

A zero-branch FAIL reported a tolerance larger than the one its decision used (err/t < 1 on a failed entry), and the worst entry was chosen in the nonzero branch only, so a column failing on a zero entry reported a passing worst (ShapeProgramming CASE4 5ea29ed7; Vera B10).

The regression-case capture kept the last judge_column call, but judge_binary32 judges a column three times and returns a fourth verdict, so a binary32 source froze D, tau and codes of the double-variant call (17 pass22 sources could not freeze, irfancn umat_viscoelastic froze with looser tolerances). freeze also removed the existing case before reading its capture, so a stop deleted the case it was to replace, and the glob over case directories matched a hidden staging directory.

The support units the transform emits carry a copy of the author's helpers, console writes included (thealanjason's lifted DSYEVJ3 keeps PRINT *, "No convergence."), and were compiled unsilenced, so Abaqus aborted the converted job at increment 1 where the silenced original did not (VISC_OGDEN_2EL / 3EL at pass22).

diagnose_transformed compiled the converted source without the support modules and so reported 'the transform emitted Fortran the compiler will not accept' for a missing module file, on every transformed_job_failed row (pass22); the solver's crash report was not kept.

redirect pointed only the first statement that opens a staged data file, so the second copy of the routine in the Jacobian-matched bundle opened the author's Windows path in the solver's scratch directory and aborted (Hunman_face, Alex x2, TendrilOfPumpkin at pass22).

The Jacobian-matched bundle held a module (NeoHookean_umat NumKind) and a main program (abuganza UMAT_Tissue_*, a bare END closing an implicit main) twice, so it did not compile and the row was recorded as a primal disagreement.

Nine pass22 rows were primal_disagreed although the Jacobian-matched control produced no comparison and the routine-level replay agreed; the gate is now not decided (primal_control_not_decided, contract 5.0.0).
A Jacobian-matched run that walked other increments gave no comparison even where the records both runs share disagree (Growth-CASE3: 1.2e-2 at t=92.7); a disagreement on shared records now stands.

beae90e bound a local named frames inside verify_one, so frames.points_for(...) -- the imported module -- raised UnboundLocalError on every row that reached it and every real pass23-prep run was a harness_error (Vera, pass23-prep blocker).
A module defined identically in both copies of the Jacobian-matched bundle was dropped from the second even when it held variables, assignments or procedures, i.e. shared state (Vera, pass23-prep).

A comparison of 0 calls was read as a primal disagreement (biofilm_visco, template_umat, neo_hookean_umat), and a disagreement on shared records that first appears after the paths part was indistinguishable from one before it (Vera, pass23-prep).

For a UMAT that USEs a module nobody supplied, the preflight reported the symptom ('anchors not located') and a card asking for a bug report, instead of naming the module to fetch (mrkearden UMAT.F90: USE Types).

The intake scanner took a *USER MATERIAL block's numbers from the pipeline's deck reader, which zero-fills a short data line and keeps only the first line of a block Abaqus rejects, so CONSTANTS=4 over two lines came back as SIGY0=0, H=0 -- a silent wrong value. It now reads the block card by card by the rules measured on Abaqus 2021.HF5 and shows an unwritten slot as not written, never as 0.
The one-page verdict rendered GREEN for a record whose six gates all read true but whose terminal state was derivative_truncated (or another state that is not fully_verified).
The compact check view printed H=None and 'Needs you: nothing' for a short *USER MATERIAL data line; it now prints 'H not written (Abaqus uses 0)' and lists the constant under Assumed.

When the pipeline's own deck reader disagreed with the card-by-card reader, check showed only a fact in the record; it now prints an amber note naming the constants. The compact view also named a constant by its position in the list of named constants instead of its slot number.

check took the typed-constants count and the state count from the older deck reader, which joins every number of a block into one list (1.,2.,3.,4. then 5.,6. counted six where Abaqus has ten slots); the intake test also used a CONSTANTS=4 block that Abaqus rejects.

When the constants had been read from the deck but the model could not be checked (finite strain, plane stress, another number of stress components), check said it could not find the numbers; it now says the constants were read and why the model is outside what is checked.

The verdict said '0 of 6 held; never measured: 6' beside a card saying the stresses agreed and no derivative disagreed, and showed NTENS, provider, tangent and PROPS to a novice; it now names the six checks, says none was run here, and uses plain words.

An empty deck was treated as no deck without a word, banners of the request and refusal cards had no colour word, ./umat-oti --help left check out of its usage line, results were written into the current directory, and doctor put the remedy inside the warning.
doctor reported a stale umat-oti on PATH as a bare warning; it now says first that all else is fine and puts the remedy on its own line, keeping exit code 1.

check printed an early GREEN corpus-record line before a RED, BLUE or AMBER verdict, showed it for an empty deck, ended a file verified in the corpus but outside the quick check as RED, printed 'Needs you: nothing' beside a verdict that was not green, and left internal words (PROPS, stress components, helpers, module) in red and blue cards.

check's line about the six checks listed passed checks as unrun, a constant used without a plain NAME = PROPS(k) line was left out of the list while the count included it, the intake listed two items under one thing, a blank run id was printed, a plane-stress file was reported as missing numbers, and a UMAT verified with another deck ended red.

The generated second-order F2EVAL (two-argument OTI functions such as x**y) divided every second-order term by 1 because the shim's get_deriv_factor returned 1.0, so the pure e1e1 and e2e2 coefficients came out doubled; the divisor now comes from oti_directions.deriv_factor. Only x**y is tested.

The deck reader published a material vector from a *USER MATERIAL block whose data lines Abaqus 2021 does not read as written (a blank line between data lines is an error, more data lines than CONSTANTS needs is an error, and a line of more than eight values is not a card); such a block is now unusable and the pairing says which rule it broke. No pairing of the 405 sources changes.

The registry decided external_dependency_unavailable from USE and INCLUDE lines only, read from a stored audit: an external CALL to a routine no file of the repository defines left a source counted as ours, and an include that was commented out or an Abaqus-supplied header counted as missing. It now applies the rule 'a callee that is not in the repository and not an Abaqus utility is external; one that is in the repository is resolved' to every source.

The D-12 init probe of the original was built with gfortran and the ifort set was used only if gfortran could not build the file, while Abaqus builds the original with ifort and its own flags, so a verdict could rest on a compiler the solver never used. The primary probe is now ifort with the Abaqus flags (-init=zero/huge/minus_huge); the gfortran set is recorded as the secondary and decides only where the primary cannot be built or run. Measured on all 166 rows that reach D-12: no verdict changed.

The transform chose the NTENS of the element from the proposals pairing while the verification chose it from the experiment planner, which picked a different deck for four sources (PhaseFieldComp 6 vs 4, Bilinear-CZM 2 vs 3, czmHealing 6 vs 2, plate_with_notch 6 vs 4): the stored transform was built for another NTENS than the element calls the UMAT with and the verification refused it. Both now read the element through experiment.deck_element.

A UMAT whose author named the 37 Abaqus arguments differently (sahmotaman subroutine umat(sigma, sv, C, ...)) was refused because the transform looked STRESS and DDSDDE up by name, although Abaqus matches the arguments by position. With exactly 37 dummies and neither STRESS nor DDSDDE, the staged copy now takes dummy k as the k-th Abaqus argument (renaming inside that routine only, other identifiers already carrying an Abaqus name moving to NAME_USR); ambiguous cases (keyword argument, CONTAINS, fixed-form line past column 72) are refused with the reason.

The dependency resolver read a free-form file with a .for suffix as fixed form, so it defined no routine, and ignored a quoted cpp #include "name", so the routines a source pulled in were invisible. It now uses the parser's own form evidence and follows a quoted #include (not #include <...>); a genuinely fixed-form .for file is still read as fixed.

A variable that only receives a clock reading (CALL CPU_TIME(COMP_TIME(1))) was promoted to the differentiated type, so the transform refused the source for handing a hypercomplex element to the timer; vendor timers (DTIME, ETIME, SECOND, CLOCK, ITIME, IDATE, TIMER) were also refused as undefined callees during helper lifting. A name whose every executable use is a timing-call argument now stays real and those timers pass through lifting; any other use of the name, and any differentiated value handed to a timer, behaves as before.

After the pipeline's deck reader began to call a block with a ninth value on a line, a blank line between data lines or extra data lines unusable, the amber note about the two readers was lost and the user was not told why no constants were taken; check now says which rule tripped and what Abaqus itself does with the block.
tests: tests/test_the_compact_check_view_fits_one_screen.py::test_each_rule_the_pipeline_reader_applies_gives_an_amber_note_with_the_rule_and_what_abaqus_does[a data line of more than eight values]

fixes.bug: check printed sentences with the word GREEN outside a green banner, and offered `umat-oti all ... --abaqus` as the way to a verified result although it only runs the file in Abaqus and records whether the job finished (the six-check comparison is not part of it); a user's --dependency-root was dropped from the suggested command.

The callee rule treated unpublished BLAS/LAPACK calls as external and trusted a partial discovery cache for CALL names, and a statement such as UserVar(i)=x was read as USE rVar, which removed or misfiled sources; library calls are now neither resolved nor external, a CALL name counts as unpublished only when confirmed absent upstream, the USE pattern needs a word boundary, and the census prints the pass23 population apart from the 14 new not-yet-attempted sources.

The registry searched only the main file for STRESS/DDSDDE assignments, so a UMAT whose body is INCLUDEd (bmmbUPF Sub_TransDisc) recorded writes_ddsdde False, and it counted modules and includes missing that the partial discovery cache lacked but the upstream tree publishes (mauro, frodal, ngrilli, xara), leaving them external; the search now follows quoted includes and upstream-published names are not missing.
